description: One company's latest nightly StockLens score: the composite score (0 to 100) and its rating word, the domain scores with their grade words, the named signals that most shaped the reading (up to three, each with its evidence), the business-model lens where one applies, and any domain that was not scored in it. Use the rating word for the company and grade words only for a domain. Bold each company's score and rating word where the answer first gives them. When findings is present, explain findings.leading, then findings.first_answer, instead of key_drivers, as findings.claim allows: strongest, they moved this score most; strongest_first, the first moved it most and the second is another factor; explained, describe what the available evidence shows, with no biggest-mover sentence. Give a finding's fact figure with its own period, which can differ from the reading's date and from another finding's. A next look is findings.next_looks[0], or the second when the first's topic was already covered for this company in the conversation or misses the person's ask; skip both when both were covered, and never mention the one you do not ask. When the person asks directly for a figure a next look carries, give it with its period, then end with the other next look's question if it is still new. Otherwise ask that one question, in its words or your own, as the answer's final line, after any link. Never state, round or hint at any figure from next_looks before the person says yes. On a yes, give only its answer as given (the company figure with its period, and for a comparison the peer figure, statistic and group), without another call and without computing anything from the figures, then stop: no other offer, menu, save or analysis. After that answer, end with the other next look's question if it is still new; otherwise stop. A finding's qualification speaks only of that trailing P/E reading: when applied is true, say in the same sentence that the company's qualifying_measure of company_figure (trailing period to period_end) eased how StockLens weighed its P/E of pe_figure against peer_median for peer_group (a blended peer mark when peer_basis is blended, never a median of companies), and how it still reads there (remaining_assessment); when applied is false, mention the figure only as context, never as easing anything, whatever the finding's own label says. When qualifying_ref names another finding in the answer, it is the same figure: say it once, keeping both findings. Never present it as a change to the overall score or a view of the stock as a whole. For a finding tied to a source, give its event_date with the event (On the Oct 29 earnings call, In its Nov 8 filing; add the year across a year boundary). An insider transaction uses its trade date. For measured activity name the event_window_start and event_window_end, never a single latest article, filing or trade. Only the current result's dated reasons and questions qualify. Never substitute the reading's date or bring an undated, stale or future event into a reason or question. On a later yes, a dated finding must still be within two calendar months of today; never fetch or substitute a different reading to revive it. Language uncertainty measures hedging; it neither proves the tone reading nor supplies an adverse finding. Answer in this order: the score and rating word with the reading's date; its available standing as a short list, Fundamental then Composite, in its market; then the supplied findings, or key_drivers if findings are absent, in their given order. Use each reason's evidence and its kind in words: SUPPORTIVE supports the reading, HEADWIND weighs against it and is never dropped or softened, MIXED cuts both ways only when its evidence carries both sides, COVERAGE_GAP is a coverage limit and NEUTRAL_NOT_MATERIAL a nonmaterial observation, neither a reason either way; then the domains in grade words. A higher Risk score means a stronger risk posture and less downside concern. Without an account, scores answer for the largest companies in each market; a signed-in account also reaches any company in its own portfolios. A result with a status other than scored is an answer, not an error; do not retry it unchanged. Relay its message; not_in_surface means the company is scored and outside the caller's reach, never that StockLens has no analysis. Then act on next_step: for ask_user, ask the person and call the named tool only if they agree; mention an offer on a scored result at most once per conversation; a list offer's rows are list_companies, for add_to_watchlist_batch. When public_page is present, you may mention it once for that company, briefly, as a link with its label, after the answer and before any closing question. Cite its canonical_url when present. Every result carries freshness; a stale result is StockLens's last computed reading for that listing, not last night's, and should be quoted with its date. When freshness.requested_ticker is present, say which listing was served and what was asked. For the evidence behind a reading, call inspect_reading with its labelled reading_ref and inspection arguments; it starts no run. Call initiate_analysis only when the person asks for a fresh analysis or agrees to one; asking for the score is not that. State available standing inside the complete reading, led by Fundamental then the coarse Composite band, with standing.universe, each band's population and standing.as_of. Each listing market is its own universe; different markets may be read side by side, never ranked on one scale. Never compute bands, quote exact numeric ranks or percentiles, or turn a standing change into a company fact. Relay standing.message and standing_definition's exclusions as given, and say so when standing is absent. For a plan_limited result, relay standing.message only when the person asks about standing, rank or comparison. One company per call; for two or more companies the person names use get_shortlist_summary. For any other ranked or filtered list call discover_stocks, and never build a ranking yourself. End with at most one forward line, and only one the result supplies: a carried next_step (an offer, or a remedy to relay), a question the person must answer first, or one question from findings.next_looks as the findings rule says. Otherwise end after the answer: do not compose a follow-up question of your own. Never offer to add, follow, save or analyze a company unless next_step offers it, quote a field, label or control name, or repeat an offer already made in this conversation. A yes to a findings question authorizes only its carried answer, never a portfolio change or fresh analysis. A successful result counts once toward the person's weekly research allowance; a RATE_LIMITED result states the limit and when it renews, so relay it and do not call again before then.

exchange.description: Exchange code (e.g. NASDAQ NYSE). Optional. Resolved automatically if omitted.

ticker.description: The company's ticker symbol (e.g. AAPL), or its name as the person gave it (e.g. Apple). One company only.

sentiment_sources_note.description: The Sentiment evidence this reading did not use and why, as one sentence to relay as given, for example: Evidence not read in this analysis: earnings calls (none found recently).

claim.description: How strongly the leading findings may be described. strongest: both moved this score most. strongest_first: the first moved it most and the second is another factor. explained: describe what the available evidence shows, with no biggest-mover sentence.

first_answer.description: One more finding the answer must carry: a counterpoint (a material finding pointing the other way) or another material finding pointing the same way. Never leave it for a question.

event_date.description: That event's own day (ISO): name it with the event, e.g. On the Oct 29 earnings call; never the reading's date.

event_kind.description: A certified discrete source (earnings_call, sec_filing, insider_transaction) or measured window (insider_activity, news_coverage, analyst_activity, edinet_large_holding).

event_window_start.description: A measured aggregate's window start (ISO); name the window, never one report.

latest_material_event_date.description: The latest material event inside an aggregate's window (ISO).

fact.description: This finding's certified figure with its own period and unit; give the figure with that period, which can differ from the reading's date.

peer_statistic.description: Which statistic of the peers peer_figure is, such as median.

applied.description: true: the qualifying figure eased how StockLens weighed this P/E. false: it changed nothing here and is context at most, never a mitigation.

peer_basis.description: observed: a median of observed peer companies. blended: a blended peer mark, never to be called a median of companies.
